real_conflicts: The proposal to apply a vertical opacity gradient to the house silhouettes (fading to 0% at the rooflines) directly undermines the focal dominance of the central figure. By dissolving the architectural mass, you remove the visual 'wall' that creates the necessary scale contrast against the tiny human figure, weakening the emotional anchor of the composition.
accepted: The proposal to increase the opacity or contrast of the road's perspective lines is fully accepted. This is the critical missing vector that will guide the viewer's eye from the bottom text up to the central figure, resolving the static nature of the current layout.
concession: I concede that the current top-heavy balance is a weakness. The massive title block does compete with the horizon line, creating a 'sandwich' effect that compresses the middle ground. I am willing to accept a reduction in the title's visual weight to improve the vertical rhythm.
compromise: Instead of fading the houses to 0% opacity (which destroys the focal anchor), we will apply a 40% opacity gradient only to the upper 20% of the house silhouettes. This preserves the solid base needed for scale while allowing the 'fading' effect requested by the imagery critic. Simultaneously, we will increase the road line contrast as I proposed to ensure the visual path remains strong despite the softer architecture.
nonnegotiable: The central figure must remain the primary focal point of the lower half. Any revision that reduces the contrast between the figure and the houses to the point where the figure is no longer immediately identifiable as the 'human presence' is a failure of the brief.
